searchText: Moving conversation from https://discordapp.com/channels/595666850260713488/749160974506000444/778096248477319178 to this channel. cc <@!273808422753796097> <@!552133098075193354> <@!187490121698770945> We *could* embrace the whole `gwei means gas price" thing and make it into official jargon... ``` gwei cap miner gwei base gwei ``` Honestly, I think a *lot* of people would get this intuitively, specifically the masses who already, as Vitalik eloquently put it, "think of gwei as some spooky thing that ends up being proportional to the amount of ETH they spend in a weird way" We could even redefine the `g` in `gwei` to mean `gas`. 😬 I kind of think many people *already* think this. well that would confuse technical people because the number itself is denominated in wei 😆 Yeah, that is fair. I'll retract my suggestion to rename `g` to `gas`. 😄 Though, we could redefine `g` to `gas` and `wei` to `price`. 😬 Since no one uses `wei` in pretty much any other context, and they *should* use `attoeth` anyway. 😛 I think people use wei when thinking about code implementations Why not just drop the fee/gwei stuff the CAP, the FEE, and the BASE easy and intuitive I like the variants around `Base gas price` and `Premiun gas price` we can definitely use `wei cap` / `miner wei` / `base wei`, but I think it is less intuitive to end users than `budget`, `inclusion premium` and `network price`, so it depends what we are optimizing for. Given that a large bit of 1559 is the UX improvement, I would be tempted to pick the most user-friendly terms over the more "technically accurate" ones (obv. the user friendly terms should be accurate, but not "engineering definition" accurate) If we just want a simple change, I still think fee -> price (except for maybe miner premium) is the way to go
